steps.head: A levy on top of tax
steps.body: The Medicare levy is charged on top of income tax. It helps fund part of the cost of Australia's public health system.

steps.head: The basic rate
steps.body: For most people the levy is 2% of taxable income. Some people get a reduction or exemption based on income.

steps.head: How it is collected
steps.body: Employers usually include it in the tax withheld from pay. The ATO works out the final amount at tax time.

steps.head: The surcharge is separate
steps.figureLabel: surcharge rate above the base tier
steps.body: The Medicare levy surcharge can apply to people without private hospital cover whose income is over a threshold.

steps.head: Insurance for the lender
steps.body: Lenders mortgage insurance (LMI) protects the lender if a borrower can't repay their home loan.

steps.head: When it applies
steps.body: LMI usually applies when the amount borrowed is more than 80% of the property's value.

steps.head: Who pays for it
steps.body: The borrower usually pays LMI as a one-off cost, even though the cover is for the lender.

steps.head: No cover for the borrower
steps.body: LMI does not benefit the borrower at all. Its job is to reduce the lender's risk when the deposit is smaller.

title:
Fixed vs variable
home loan rates

steps.head: Fixed: locked in
steps.body: A fixed rate stays the same for a set period, usually between one and five years.

steps.head: Variable: can move
steps.body: A variable rate can go up or down over time. The lender decides when to change it and by how much.

steps.head: Repayments differ
steps.body: Fixed repayments stay steady for the fixed period. Variable repayments shift whenever the rate changes.

steps.head: The split option
steps.body: A split loan fixes the rate on part of the balance and leaves the rest variable, mixing both features.

steps.head: Pay in instalments
steps.body: BNPL services split a purchase into smaller repayments over a set period.

steps.head: Now under credit law
steps.figureLabel: year BNPL came under credit law
steps.body: Since 10 June 2025, BNPL contracts have been covered by the National Credit Code.

steps.head: A licence is required
steps.body: Providers need an Australian credit licence and membership of AFCA, the financial complaints authority.

steps.head: Modified lending checks
steps.body: Low-cost credit like BNPL can follow modified responsible lending rules rather than the full set for loans.

steps.head: A share of profits
steps.body: A dividend is a payment a company makes to its shareholders, usually out of its profits.

steps.head: Often twice a year
steps.body: Many ASX companies pay an interim and a final dividend each year. Some also pay a one-off special dividend.

steps.head: The key dates
steps.body: The record date sets who gets paid. Shares acquired from the ex-dividend date on don't come with that dividend.

steps.head: Price can adjust
steps.body: A share price may move up as the ex-dividend date nears, then fall once the shares trade ex-dividend.

steps.head: The size of the economy
steps.body: Gross domestic product (GDP) is the total value of goods and services produced in Australia over a period.

steps.head: Measured every quarter
steps.body: The ABS publishes GDP each quarter, so growth can be tracked through the year.

steps.head: Real vs nominal
steps.body: Nominal GDP counts the dollar value. Real GDP strips out price changes to show the change in volume produced.

steps.head: Three ways to count it
steps.body: GDP can be measured by production, income or spending. The ABS generally uses the average of the three.

steps.head: Debt tied to living costs
steps.body: Each year a HELP debt is adjusted by indexation, so it keeps pace with changes in the cost of living.

steps.head: When it happens
steps.body: Indexation is applied on 1 June. It only applies to HELP debt that is more than 11 months old.

steps.head: How the rate is set
steps.body: The rate is the lower of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) and the Wage Price Index (WPI), backdated to 2023.

steps.head: The 2026 rate
steps.body: The indexation rate applied to HELP debts on 1 June 2026 was 2.8%, down from 3.2% in 2025.

title:
How the jobless
rate is measured

steps.head: A monthly survey
steps.body: The ABS Labour Force Survey covers about 24,000 homes, or roughly 50,000 people, every month.

steps.head: One hour counts as a job
steps.body: Anyone who did at least one hour of paid work in the survey week is counted as employed.

steps.head: Who counts as unemployed
steps.body: People without work who looked for a job in the past four weeks and were available to start.

steps.head: The rate itself
steps.body: Unemployed people as a share of the labour force, which is everyone employed plus everyone unemployed.

title:
How tax brackets
work in Australia

steps.head: A tax-free first slice
steps.body: Australian residents pay no income tax on the first $18,200 of taxable income each year.

steps.head: Rates rise in steps
steps.body: For 2026–27, each dollar from $18,201 to $45,000 is taxed at 15c, down from 16c the year before.

steps.head: Only the slice is taxed
steps.body: Moving into a higher bracket only changes the rate on dollars above that line. Lower slices keep their lower rates.

steps.head: The top rate
steps.body: Income over $190,000 is taxed at 45c per dollar. The 2% Medicare levy sits on top of these rates.

steps.head: Pay goes in before tax
steps.body: Under salary sacrifice, an employee agrees to send part of their pre-tax pay into super instead of their bank account.

steps.head: Taxed in the fund
steps.figureLabel: tax on it inside the super fund
steps.body: The sacrificed amount skips PAYG withholding. The fund taxes it at 15%, generally lower than marginal tax rates.

steps.head: It counts toward a cap
steps.body: Salary sacrifice and employer contributions share the concessional cap, which rose from $30,000 to $32,500 on 1 July 2026.

steps.head: Employer super stays put
steps.body: The employer still pays its full compulsory super. Sacrificed amounts are extra and do not count toward it.

steps.head: Two rates on one loan
steps.body: Home loans come with two rates: the advertised interest rate and a comparison rate.

steps.head: Fees folded in
steps.body: The comparison rate rolls the interest rate and most fees and charges into a single percentage figure.

steps.head: Why the two differ
steps.body: A loan with a low rate but high fees can end up with a comparison rate well above its headline rate.

steps.head: Not every cost is in it
steps.body: It covers most fees, not all. A lender’s Key Facts Sheet shows a personalised comparison rate for the amount borrowed.

title:
The first home
super saver scheme

steps.head: Saving inside super
steps.body: The FHSS scheme lets first home savers make voluntary super contributions, then later release them for a home.

steps.head: Yearly and total limits
steps.body: Up to $15,000 of eligible contributions count each financial year, with a total limit of $50,000 across all years.

steps.head: What comes back out
steps.body: All after-tax contributions count, but only 85% of before-tax ones like salary sacrifice, plus some deemed earnings.

steps.head: Tax on the way out
steps.figureLabel: FHSS tax offset on the release
steps.body: Released amounts are taxed with a 30% offset. The ATO determination has to be requested before settlement.

steps.head: Orders queue up first
steps.body: From 7am Sydney time, orders can be entered but nothing is matched yet. They wait in a queue.

steps.head: An opening auction
steps.body: Just before 10am, a short auction sets each opening price from the queued orders, then normal trading begins.

steps.head: Normal trading
steps.body: Through the day, orders are matched continuously whenever prices meet. That stops at 4pm.

steps.head: A closing auction
steps.body: After ten minutes for orders to adjust, a closing single price auction from 4:10pm sets each closing price.

title:
What the Wage
Price Index tracks

steps.head: The price of labour
steps.body: The ABS Wage Price Index tracks how hourly rates of pay change over time, a bit like the CPI does for prices.

steps.head: Same jobs, every quarter
steps.body: About 3,000 businesses report pay for around 18,000 matched jobs, so the same jobs are compared each quarter.

steps.head: Mix changes stripped out
steps.body: Shifts in who is working, like more high-paid roles, are removed, so the index shows pure changes in pay rates.

steps.head: What is left out
steps.body: The headline index excludes bonuses and on-costs like payroll tax and super. It comes out about 7 weeks after each quarter.

steps.head: Locked rate, locked term
steps.body: A term deposit holds money for a set period, often one month to five years, at an interest rate fixed at the start.

steps.head: Getting out early
steps.body: Withdrawing early can mean up to 31 days’ notice, a fee, and only part of the interest, or none at all.

steps.head: At maturity
steps.body: The provider makes contact when the term ends. If nothing changes, the deposit may roll into a new term at a new rate.

steps.head: Government backed
steps.body: If an APRA-regulated bank, credit union or building society fails, the scheme covers deposits up to $250,000.

steps.head: Price over earnings
steps.body: A P/E ratio divides a company’s share price by its earnings per share over the past twelve months.

steps.head: Earnings per share
steps.body: Earnings per share is the company’s profit divided by the number of shares on issue.

steps.head: Reading the number
steps.body: A higher P/E means the market is paying more for each dollar of a company’s yearly earnings.

steps.head: Linked to market cap
steps.body: Market cap is the share price times shares on issue, so P/E also equals market cap divided by total profit.
